A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning, attention masking, activation patching, and retrieval-head analyses using Llama-3 and Mistral on three tasks.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional unfine-tuned baseline results and revised retrieval-head analyses.

M1.justification: The synthetic-data construction procedures, LoRA configurations, retrieval and insight scores, masking, and cross-model patching remain unchanged. v2 clarifies head identification and patching implementation without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MDQA, linear three-hop MuSiQue, SummHay Citation, and their existing synthetic and limited-data variants. The newly explained T-REx filtering describes the existing MuSiQue limited-data condition, rather than added coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds a Non-FT comparator for both models across all three tasks. Existing real-data and synthetic-data comparisons, and random-head controls in intervention experiments, are retained.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same context lengths, model sizes, sample counts, 90/10 splits, LoRA settings, and greedy decoding. Added descriptions of padding, subset selection, and patching disclose previously unspecified details rather than explicitly revise settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds diagnostic heatmaps comparing head locations across real and synthetic variants (Figures 7–9), supporting the discussion of matching heads by index. Tables 14–16 also add explicit recall–F1 correlations for all-module LoRA. Masking, patching, and the all-module comparison already existed.

E5.justification: Both versions average random-head masking over three samples and retain the same statistical reporting practices. Revised Spearman coefficients are result changes; no new seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 5, 6, 8, 9, 14, and 15 substantially revise head-recall matrices. For example, Llama MuSiQue H,L recall against real heads changes from 0.87 to 0.66. Its recall–F1 correlation changes from 0.81 to 0.75, while Mistral MDQA changes from -0.27 to 0.16 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 4). v2 also adds Non-FT scores, swaps MDQA L2/L3 score/count associations in Tables 5 and 8, and changes the Simplified/High SummHay random-patch entry in Table 11 from 0.35 to 0.3. Most downstream F1 and patching results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The dataset formalization, score equations, and intersection/complement definitions remain mathematically equivalent. Per-example wording and indicator-bracket edits add clarification, not new definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: A central structural finding is substantially narrowed. v1's abstract describes synthetic heads as mostly subsets, and Section 4.1 asserts strict containment for MDQA and MuSiQue. v2's abstract instead claims high overlap, its introduction emphasizes fewer heads, and Section 4.1 qualifies subset-like behavior by task. The necessity, insufficiency, and performance-correlation claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 expands the upstream-representation hypothesis into an explanation involving synthetic-to-real distribution mismatch. Figure 6 newly interprets late retrieval heads as supporting final answer copying and middle-layer insight heads as serving intermediate processing. It also qualifies the generality of subset patterns.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds data examples, subset proportions, and the MuSiQue T-REx selection rule; Section 2.2 specifies its repeated-text padding. Appendix F identifies Baukit and explains patching locations and input-only patching without output-token interventions. Conversely, the reproducibility statement removes the planned code-release URL while retaining the release promise.

R1.justification: v2 adds Elsahar et al. (2018), the T-REx reference, to explain MuSiQue subset provenance. The related-work argument remains essentially unchanged; the RULER publication update concerns the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted rewrites to the background, synthetic-data framing, retrieval-head explanations, and captions. It subdivides Appendix C and consolidates patching appendices, with full-fine-tuning material moving from H to G. The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with three multi-panel real-versus-synthetic heatmap grids and two data-example boxes. Figure 1 is reformatted, recall-table rows and columns are reorganized, and the symbolic-example figure and recall-correlation table move into appendices. Existing masking and cosine-similarity plots are relocated without changing their plotted results.

improvement.justification: v2 improves evidence–claim alignment by replacing strict-containment claims with qualified overlap, adds an unfine-tuned comparison, and makes subset selection and patching more reproducible. These gains are limited: most experiments remain unchanged, the planned code-release URL disappears, and Section 4.1 still mismatches the symbolic case with Table 6. Overall, the clearer documentation and more defensible claim scope provide a modest net improvement.
